absent: How processor side logging enablement, manual protect mode, eager reduction control, and leaf dirty clearing are implemented is not shown.
Internals of shadow write protection, collapsible detection, and shadow reduction handlers plus reverse map iterator mechanics are not shown.
Two dimensional iterator start and advance, rescheduling and yield safety, atomic entry update, and root validity rules are not shown.
Page statistics update, table accounting policy, and debug counter semantics beyond increment are not shown.
Architecture ranged invalidation capabilities and ordering guarantees with slots serialization are not shown.
Slot lookup, address space selection, and guest frame to host mapping establishment are not shown.

findings.text: A slot wide write revocation service exists that clears guest write permission over every mapping that belongs to one memory slot, starting at a caller chosen page size. It covers both the reverse map based shadow engine and the two dimensional paging engine when each is active.

A slot wide large mapping reduction service exists that attempts to replace mappings larger than a caller chosen size with smaller ones. It applies to both paging engines when active and explicitly leaves translation invalidation to later protection handling.

A slot wide large mapping restoration service exists that discards small collapsible mappings so that larger mappings can be rebuilt after fine grained write tracking ends. It acts on both paging engines when active.

Three two dimensional paging helpers operate on one slot within one address space identifier: one clears hardware write permission above a minimum size, one attempts large mapping reduction toward a target size, and one restores large mappings. Each walks every valid root for that address space.

Two translation invalidation helpers exist: one invalidates a guest frame interval with fallback to full invalidation when ranged invalidation is unavailable, and one invalidates a whole slot by delegating to the interval form.

Memory slot creation, relocation, removal and flag mutation converge on one handler that reconciles requested logging and access attributes with existing shadow state. It synchronizes processor side logging on toggles and then either restores large mappings or establishes write tracking with invalidation.

Write tracking for a slot has two steady postures. When tracking is turned off the system seeks to rebuild large mappings. When tracking is turned on the system optionally reduces large mappings eagerly, adjusts processor dirty state and write permission according to processor logging support, and invalidates remote translations. Read only slots and lifecycle operations remain in a no further work posture.

Only a flag only mutation on a writable slot proceeds to tracking establishment or teardown. Lifecycle operations and read only slots require no per mapping work because mappings are either absent or already discarded, and any surviving flag only mutation is expected to be a logging toggle.

Two dimensional write protection visits entries at or above a minimum size within a slot interval and affects solely present terminal entries that currently permit hardware writes. It clears that permission atomically, retries on contention, and reports whether any entry changed.

Splitting derives each child entry from its large parent by adding the child index scaled position offset, dropping the large size attribute at the smallest size, and refreshing execution permission according to role access when the non executable large page mitigation is active.

Permission changes preserve access tracking state by temporarily restoring tracked entries to normal form, applying set and clear masks with a disjointness expectation, and then reapplying tracking encoding. Entries that already use hardware dirty support keep their accessed handling unchanged.

A newly linked paging level is represented by a present writable entry that carries architecture permission and encryption masks plus accessed state. The accessed representation differs depending on whether hardware dirty support is disabled.
Linking a new two dimensional paging structure charges one page table page to the virtual machine and, under a debug option, increments a per virtual machine page counter.
Reverse map based reduction proceeds from the largest size down toward but excluding the target size, so that multi level large mappings are recursively reduced to the requested granularity.
Two dimensional reduction relies on parent before child visitation to ensure that mappings several sizes above the target are progressively reduced during a single traversal.
Restoration for reverse map structures scans from the smallest size up to one below the maximum and invalidates the slot when any collapsible entry was discarded.

Reverse map range traversal mandates exclusive hold of the memory management lock, cooperatively yields on scheduling need or lock contention, and can emit interval invalidation for accumulated changes before yielding. The slot scoped wrapper fixes the interval to the full slot extent.

Slot wide protection, reduction and restoration use exclusive hold for reverse map structures and shared hold for two dimensional structures. Whole slot invalidation mandates hold of the slots mutex. Two dimensional reduction performs table allocation outside locks and read sections, then resumes traversal.

A fresh child paging structure records a decremented level role derived from its parent, the starting guest frame, a link to the parent entry, and a marker denoting two dimensional ownership, with list linkage and a reverse lookup association established at creation.

After establishing write tracking the system invalidates remote translations unconditionally and outside the memory management lock, relying on ordering before user space consumption rather than on entry writability. Consumers must not treat a non writable entry as proof that processors cannot write, owing to stale entries and deferred permission changes.

Large mapping reduction performs no invalidation itself. Safety rests on children inheriting write and dirty posture from the parent and on later protection handling deciding invalidation from the split form. Replacing a large entry by a table reference without invalidation preserves translation.

Two dimensional reduction preallocates one child table at a time and may abort a root walk with an out of memory report while leaving earlier splits installed. A preallocated table that loses a race and remains unused is released through the paging structure reclamation path.

The slot flag KVM_MEM_LOG_DIRTY_PAGES selects write tracking, KVM_MEM_READONLY selects read only posture, and KVM_MR_FLAGS_ONLY distinguishes attribute mutation from lifecycle operations. Size selection uses PG_LEVEL_4K and PG_LEVEL_2M with KVM_MAX_HUGEPAGE_LEVEL as the upper bound.

Hardware write permission is denoted by PT_WRITABLE_MASK, size attribute by PT_PAGE_SIZE_MASK, and presence by PT_PRESENT_MASK alongside shadow permission and accessed masks. Child fanout uses SPTE_ENT_PER_PAGE.
